title: Al-Kahf 1 to 10: the young people of the cave and reflection: rule card and examples
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
unit: Spring 1: Tajweed mastery and Al-Kahf consolidation
source: Written for quran/y11 lesson 12 (Pupil PDF worksheet: Al-Kahf 1 to 10 rule card and examples)
intro: Lesson 12. Read the rule and say every example aloud. Point to each word in your mushaf. Then answer the questions.

panels.title: Lessons from 18:9 to 10
points: Ask for mercy and right guidance

arabic.text: إِذْ أَوَى ٱلْفِتْيَةُ إِلَى ٱلْكَهْفِ فَقَالُوا۟ رَبَّنَآ ءَاتِنَا مِن لَّدُنكَ رَحْمَةًۭ وَهَيِّئْ لَنَا مِنْ أَمْرِنَا رَشَدًۭا (١٠)

panels.title: Recite in turns
points: Whole ten ayat round the class

keywords.def: a trial or test of faith

questions.q: In the portal response box, write a paragraph: 'How can the first ten ayat of Al-Kahf help a young Muslim today?' (Point, Evidence, Explain, Link).
questions.a: Point: they strengthen faith. Evidence: 18:10 du'a; 18:7 the test. Explain: turning to Allah and seeing the world as a test. Link: protection from fitnah.

questions.q: 18:8 says the earth's adornment will become ...
Complete your paragraph, then recite 18:1 to 10 to a partner (pupil PDF rubric). Today's rota group recites 18:6 to 10 to the teacher.
questions.a: Paragraph complete; partner rubric with a target.

questions.q: Extend: memorise the du'a of 18:10 with its meaning.
Stretch: explain 'which of them is best in deed' (18:7): best, not most.
questions.a: Quality and sincerity of deeds matter, not only quantity.

questions.q: 18:7 says Allah made what is on the earth an adornment ...
options: to test who is best in deeds
questions.a: A) to test who is best in deeds. 18:7: 'that We may test them as to which of them is best in deed'.

questions.q: Memorising the first ten ayat of Al-Kahf protects from ...
Think again: The people of the cave were young. What tests (fitan) do young Muslims face today, and what did the youths do?
questions.a: Pressure on faith, distraction, wrong company; they turned to Allah, asked for mercy and guidance, and kept together.
